title: AHB Pipeline Stall vs AXI Channel-Local Stall
description: A scheduling example contrasts an AHB data-phase wait that also holds the overlapping address phase with an AXI W-channel stall that does not prevent independent AW handshakes; it is not a mandated latency comparison.

annotations.message: Both examples begin presenting requests. This visual compares interface scheduling only; target latency and buffering remain implementation-dependent.
AHB completes D1 while showing A2. AXI accepts AW2 and W1 on their independent channels.
AHB_HREADY is LOW during D2, so the overlapping A3 address phase is not accepted and must remain stable. AXI still accepts AW3 even though W2 is backpressured.
The AHB address/control and data phases remain frozen. AXI WVALID and WDATA=W2 remain stable while AW is already free.
AHB_HREADY returns HIGH, completing D2 and accepting held address A3. AXI_WREADY returns HIGH and accepts W2.
Both data paths make progress again. AXI's advantage here is isolation of the AW handshake from the W stall, not a universal throughput guarantee.
